newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt prices fall on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt prices fall on selling pressure.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities fell on Friday as market sentiment turned bearish on fears of central bank sale of newly-issued 10-year bonds, dealers said.
The government on Wednesday issued 50 billion rupees of 10-year bonds in a private placement deal with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 13.05 percent.

Dealers said the issue was at a yield higher than secondary market yields of around 12.60 percent for stocks of the same maturity and had led to fears that the central bank wanted a correction in the yield curve.
"So far the RBI has not sold the bond but the market is definitely apprehensive that it will do so sooner or later," said a dealer.
"Even trading banks are selling..this is an indication that sentiment is down," he said.
Other dealers said the fall in prices could be a correction after a sustained bull-run in the securities market.
"Prices have definitely rising for more than a month now," said another dealer. "There was bound to be a correction.
Dealers said there was selling pressure in short and medium-term stocks but longer dated stocks seemed to be stable.
"The 13.65 percent 2007 actually bucked the trend and rose to 105.15 rupees from 104," said a dealer. "But it was a single deal."
The 13.80 percent 2002 stock saw a sharp fall in prices to 107.40 rupees from Thursday's 108.50, dealers said.
Other stocks which fell included the 13.40 percent 1999 which fell to 107.30 from 107.65, the 13.50 percent 1997 to 102.26 from 102.38 and the 13.82 percent 2002 to 107.60 from 107.65.
Dealers said treasury bills maturing in July yielded 4.75 percent, January 1998 bill 8.05-8.10 percent and APril bills 8.65-8.90 percent.
One-month certificates of deposit and commercial paper were quoted at 8.0 percent in the secondary market.
Dealers said call money was inactive at 0.10-0.25 percent as it was the reporting day.
Three-month money was trade at 8.25 percent, dealers said.
